name: tfscript-vscode
description: Language support for tfscript, TinyFugue's macro language: diagnostics and command-name completion, plus syntax highlighting for .tf files.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Only reports diagnostics and completions for the open file; runs no workspace-authored code or config.

tfscript.entryFiles.markdownDescription: Files tf loads after `stdlib.tf`, in order — normally your tfrc. The server follows their `/load` and `/require` lines to learn which macros each file can see. Relative paths are relative to the workspace folder; `~` is your home directory. When empty: a `.tfrc`, `tfrc` or `tfrc.tf` at the folder root, else `~/.tfrc`, else `~/tfrc`.

tfscript.contexts.markdownDescription: Named ways tf might be started, each a list of entry files like `#tfscript.entryFiles#`: for example `{ "wotmud": ["wot.tfrc"], "diku": ["diku.tfrc"] }`. A file loaded by several is seen through `#tfscript.activeContext#`; one the active context doesn't load is seen through the first context that does. Empty: one context, `default`, from `#tfscript.entryFiles#`.

tfscript.activeContext.markdownDescription: Which of `#tfscript.contexts#` is active. Set it from the status bar item shown for tf files (**tfscript: Choose Load Context**). Empty: the first.

tfscript.libraryPath.markdownDescription: tf's library directory (`TFLIBDIR`), the one holding `stdlib.tf`. Its files are read at runtime for hover docs and for `/require` targets. When empty: the `TFLIBDIR` environment variable.

tfscript.tfPath.markdownDescription: `TFPATH` as tf starts with it: directories searched for relative `/load` paths. As in tf, a non-empty `TFPATH` replaces the library directory as the fallback, so include it here if your scripts `/require` library files. When empty: the `TFPATH` environment variable.

tfscript.workingDirectory.markdownDescription: The directory tf runs in. Relative `/load` paths are tried here first — not beside the loading file. When empty: the workspace folder.

tfscript.diagnostics.unresolvedLoads.markdownDescription: Warn about a `/load` or `/require` on the load path whose file tf wouldn't find, listing where it would look.

tfscript.diagnostics.undefinedMacros.markdownDescription: Warn about a `/name` command that calls a macro defined nowhere: not a tf command, and not defined in any file on the load path, in the workspace or in tf's library. A macro defined in a workspace or library file the load path doesn't reach is a note, with a fix that adds the `/require`. When a load that might define it can't be followed (its path is built from a variable this can't see), the warning becomes a note naming that load. Macros made while tf runs (`/eval /def`, a file loaded some other way) aren't seen: list them in `#tfscript.diagnostics.ignoreMacros#`.

tfscript.codeLens.references.markdownDescription: Show how many references each `/def` has above it (calls and `${name}` substitutions in the files on its load path), opening them in the references peek when clicked.

tfscript.diagnostics.ignoreMacros.markdownDescription: Macro names the undefined-macro check leaves alone, ignoring case; `*` matches any run of characters (`wot_*`).

tfscript.homeDirectory.markdownDescription: What `~` means in load paths (tf's `HOME`). Useful when tf runs somewhere else, such as WSL or a container. When empty: your home directory.

tf.markdownDescription: An absolute path as tf sees it, such as `/wotmud`.

local.markdownDescription: The folder here that it is, absolute or relative to the workspace folder.

tfscript.pathMappings.markdownDescription: Where tf's paths are on this machine, when tf runs somewhere else (a container, WSL, another host): `[{ "tf": "/wotmud", "local": "C:/Users/me/wotmud" }]`. Absolute paths in `/load` and `/require`, and in the `TFPATH` and `HOME` a script sets, go through it, as do the other path settings when written as tf's paths.

tfscript.variables.markdownDescription: Variables with a value when tf starts, as if `/set` after `stdlib.tf`: set in the environment, by a tfrc outside the workspace, or by a default this check can't work out, such as `/if (x =~ "") /set x=...%; /endif`. For example `{ "wotmud_repo_dir": "/wotmud" }`. Values are as tf sees them, so paths go through `#tfscript.pathMappings#`. A value here stands through a `/set` of it inside an `/if` or `/while`; a `/set` that always runs replaces it.

enumDescriptions: A tf that loads a file saved with CRLF line endings like an LF one, and fixes three bugs in macro bodies: a ?: that crashed tf, a comma in $[...] that lost text, and /else running after a true /if and a true /elseif.
tfscript.tfBuild.markdownDescription: Which tf the scripts run in, where builds differ in what a script does. With `fork`, a `\` before a CRLF line ending continues the line, and extracting a variable is offered where upstream's bugs ruled it out.

scripts.build: npm --prefix ../.. run build && npm --prefix ../.. run bundle:claude-code && tsc -p . && node scripts/copy-server.js
scripts.package: npm run build && npm test && vsce package -o tfscript-vscode.vsix
